title: The Périgord Noir, Slowly

bestPeriod.note: Truffle and foie gras season runs November to March, outside this window; these dates instead catch the walnut harvest and the start of autumn markets without July's crowds.

summary: A slow week between Sarlat's market streets and the Vézère's river villages, with one relocation, walnut mills and honey-stone bastides.
hook: This is a week for a single valley, walked twice rather than four valleys walked once. Sarlat's golden stone streets, the cliff villages on the Dordogne, and the quiet Romanesque churches of the Vézère all sit within a short drive of each other, close enough that the right pace is no pace at all.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Under 200 km of driving all week, flat river walks, occasional hilltop climbs
snapshot.Getting There: 20 min from Bergerac Airport to Sarlat; TGV to Bordeaux then a rental car (2h15)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Slow travellers, food-focused couples, families who like rivers more than motorways

itinerary.title: Settling into Sarlat-la-Canéda
itinerary.morning: Arrive and walk into the old town through Rue de la République. The daily produce market fills the Sainte-Marie hall, a deconsecrated church redesigned as a covered market by Jean Nouvel in 2001, every morning except Monday.
itinerary.afternoon: Wander Rue de la Salamandre and Rue des Consuls, lined with 14th- to 17th-century hôtels particuliers in honey-coloured limestone, then the Lanterne des Morts beside the cathedral.
itinerary.evening: Dinner near Place du Marché aux Oies, the old goose market square, on Périgourdine staples: confit, walnut salad, Cabécou.
itinerary.dayStats: 3 km walking · relocations: 0 · market: Sarlat daily produce market (except Monday), 08:00-13:00.

itinerary.title: Sarlat's Saturday market and a walnut mill
itinerary.morning: Time this day for a Saturday: the market spreads through every street of the old town, 08:00-13:00, alongside a smaller Wednesday version. Walnuts, cèpes in season, foie gras, duck confit and Cabécou cheese fill the stalls.
itinerary.afternoon: A 15-minute drive to Sainte-Nathalène for the Moulin de la Tour, a 19th-century stone mill still pressing walnut and hazelnut oil on its original millstones, with tastings at the end of the visit.
itinerary.evening: Return to Sarlat for a quiet dinner; the town empties out fast once the market stalls are gone.
itinerary.dayStats: 20 km round trip, 30 min driving · relocations: 0.

itinerary.title: La Roque-Gageac and Domme
itinerary.morning: La Roque-Gageac, built into a cliff face above the Dordogne, has a small riverside market on Friday mornings in season. Walk the single street and the troglodyte fort cut into the rock above it, then take a gabare river boat, flat-bottomed barges once used to carry goods downriver, now running short scenic loops.
itinerary.afternoon: Domme, a bastide founded in 1281 on a limestone spur, has its own Thursday morning market on Place de la Halle. Walk through the Porte des Tours gate, stand at the Belvédère de la Barre for the whole valley in one view, and cool off in the show cave below the town, the Grotte de Domme.
itinerary.dayStats: 26 km round trip, 45 min driving · relocations: 0 · markets: La Roque-Gageac (Friday, seasonal), Domme (Thursday, 08:00-13:00).

itinerary.title: Beynac-et-Cazenac
itinerary.morning: Château de Beynac, an 11th- to 13th-century fortress on a sheer cliff above the river, is one of the best-preserved in the valley and was used as a filming location for its unbroken medieval silhouette. Climb the narrow lanes below it slowly, there is no reason to rush a village this small.
itinerary.afternoon: A short riverside walk toward La Balme or a second gabare run from Beynac's own landing, looking back up at the château from the water.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Beynac, then back to Sarlat to pack for tomorrow's move.
itinerary.dayStats: 24 km round trip, 40 min driving · relocations: 0.

itinerary.title: Relocating to the Vézère: Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère
itinerary.morning: The one relocation of the week: Sarlat to Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère, 35 km, about 40 minutes on quiet D-roads. The village is listed among France's most beautiful, built around a Romanesque church, Saint-Léonce, from the 11th and 12th centuries, and a bend in the river with a shallow beach.
itinerary.afternoon: Check into the new base and walk the riverside path past the private Château de la Salle and Château de Clérans, visible only from outside.
itinerary.evening: A slow dinner in the village; there is little else to do here after dark, which is the point.

itinerary.title: Montignac market and Vézère prehistory
itinerary.morning: Montignac-Lascaux holds a market on Wednesday and Saturday mornings along the riverbank, smaller and less touristy than Sarlat's.
itinerary.afternoon: Lascaux IV, the Centre International de l'Art Pariétal designed by Snøhetta in 2016, needs a timed ticket, book at least a few weeks ahead in summer. Alternatively, or as a second stop, the Renaissance Château de Losse near Thonac sits directly on the Vézère with formal gardens running down to the water.
itinerary.evening: Dinner back in Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère or Montignac.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km round trip, 25 min driving · relocations: 0 · market: Montignac, Wednesday and Saturday, 08:00-13:00.

itinerary.title: Les Eyzies and departure
itinerary.morning: Les Eyzies-de-Tayac, self-styled capital of prehistory, holds the Musée National de Préhistoire, built into the cliff itself by architect Jean-Pierre Buffi in 2004, and the Abri Pataud rock shelter beside it.
itinerary.afternoon: Last stop for foie gras, walnut oil and duck products at a producer shop in Les Eyzies or back through Sarlat, depending on your route to Bergerac.
itinerary.evening: If the flight is late, a final dinner in Bergerac's own old town near the Cyrano statue before the airport.
itinerary.dayStats: 25 km to Les Eyzies, then 55 km to Bergerac, about 1h15 total driving · relocations: 0 (departure).

accommodationStrategy.name: La Hoirie
accommodationStrategy.location: Route de la Chapelle-Péchaud, just outside Sarlat
accommodationStrategy.description: A 17th-century manor with its own park and pool a five-minute drive from Sarlat's old town, useful for Days 1-4 when you want quiet evenings after a day of walking cobbles and market crowds. Ask for a room facing the garden, not the car park.

accommodationStrategy.name: La Villa des Consuls
accommodationStrategy.description: A 16th-century town house on a quiet street inside the old town walls, close enough to the Sainte-Marie market hall to walk over for coffee before the Saturday crowds build. Good for travellers who want to be inside Sarlat rather than driving in each morning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Moulin de la Beune
accommodationStrategy.description: An old mill building on the Beune, a short walk from the Vézère confluence and the prehistory museum, and a 15-minute drive from Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère, a good last-night option if your flight leaves early from Bergerac.

logistics.emergency: 112 for all services; French mountain and river rescue also routes through 112.
logistics.money: Cards work in restaurants and larger shops; carry cash for market stalls and small producers.
logistics.health: The Vézère's beach at Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère is unsupervised, check current speed after rain before letting children swim.

other.label: A car is essential
other.text: Public transport between these villages is sparse to nonexistent; rent from Bergerac or Bordeaux and plan on under 200 km for the whole week.

other.label: Parking in Sarlat
other.text: The old town is largely pedestrian on market mornings; use the Sainte-Marie or Plaine de la Rode car parks and walk in, do not attempt to drive into the centre on a Saturday before 13:00.

other.label: Market rhythm
other.text: Sarlat: daily except Monday, biggest Saturday. Domme: Thursday mornings. La Roque-Gageac: Friday mornings, seasonal. Montignac: Wednesday and Saturday mornings. Build the week around whichever falls where you are.

other.label: Truffle and foie gras seasonality
other.text: Fresh Périgord black truffle (Tuber melanosporum) is a December-to-March product, sold at winter truffle markets in Sarlat and at Sainte-Alvère's Monday afternoon truffle market; outside those months, shops sell preserved or frozen truffle and jarred foie gras rather than fresh.

other.label: Opening-hour trap
other.text: Small village shops and even some château ticket desks close for lunch, typically 12:30-14:00, and many are shut on Mondays outside peak summer.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for all services; French mountain and river rescue also routes through 112.

proTips: Arrive so that Day 2 lands on a Saturday; Sarlat's market is markedly bigger than the Wednesday version and worth building the whole week around.
Reach Beynac and La Roque-Gageac by 09:30, both fill with coach groups from Sarlat and Périgueux by midday.
The Moulin de la Tour tasting is free with a visit; buy the walnut oil there rather than in a Sarlat shop, it is noticeably fresher.
Book Lascaux IV tickets for a late-morning slot; the light in the reconstructed caves reads better before the afternoon groups thicken the queue.
The Grotte de Domme stays a cool 13°C year-round, a good midday escape from a hot Périgord afternoon.
Château de Losse draws far fewer visitors than Beynac despite being just as photogenic from the river.

packingNotes: Flat, grippy shoes, Sarlat's cobbles and Domme's ramparts are uneven underfoot.
A light layer for the show caves and mill interiors, which stay around 12-14°C even in July.
Swimwear for the Vézère beach at Saint-Léon-sur-Vézère.
A reusable tote for market shopping; stallholders weigh and wrap, they do not bag.
Cash in small notes and coins for market stalls and church donation boxes.
A hat and sun protection for the exposed viewpoints at Domme and the Belvédère de la Barre.
A cool bag if you plan to buy foie gras or fresh duck products to take home.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Lascaux IV is sold out for your date.** Font-de-Gaume near Les Eyzies runs limited daily tickets to see original polychrome paintings, a genuine and often quieter alternative.
**Sarlat's car parks are full on Saturday morning.** Park at Plaine de la Rode and walk the ten minutes in rather than circling for a closer spot.
**A château or mill closes for a private event.** Most post updates on their own websites the week before; check the morning you plan to go rather than assuming a summer schedule holds.
**Midsummer heat makes midday walking unpleasant.** Shift to a Domme-cave or museum interior between 13:00 and 16:00, and save exposed viewpoints for morning or early evening.
**Narrow D-roads and blind bends catch first-time drivers.** Speeds are naturally low; treat every hilltop bend as blind and give way at unmarked village junctions.
